meta.title: The YouTuber a Casino Paid to Stop Posting
meta.working_title: A Casino Paid This YouTuber to Stop Posting
meta.device: A red 'KICKED OUT' stamp thumps onto the screen every time a door closes on Jack (supermarket, Kick, Kick again, PGA Tour, Shuffle), and a running BANNED list (a clipboard top-right) gains one line each time. The list is the spine of the video.
meta.style: Stormi 2D house style (Gumball-style rig characters on painted plates, same engine as Prime/Pattinson/Gulf Kings/Whatnot). Real people stylised, no likeness, no real logos (no Kick, Shuffle, McLaren, PGA or Walmart logos; names only as plain text in our own font). Allegations always phrased as allegations; outcomes not reported are said to be unreported. No slurs shown or spoken.
meta.source: YouTube reference (Sid Montage, 'Why the Internet Hates Jack Doherty', youtu.be/TvpFRx2klyk, transcript pulled via Pushpam's Chrome 28 Nov 2026), itself based on NBC News, Car Throttle/Miami New Times, Tubefilter, Dexerto, Golf Magic, IBTimes UK, MyMMANews. Research only; original script, en-GB.

shots.vo: In October twenty twenty-six, a casino company did something no sponsor had ever done. It paid a YouTuber with fifteen million subscribers... to stop posting.
shots.visual: Casino-style boardroom at night: a briefcase of cash slides across a table towards a phone that shows a YouTube-style channel page (15M); the phone screen goes dark.
shots.anim: Briefcase slides, cash flutters; phone screen fades to black; '15M SUBSCRIBERS' counter.

shots.vo: The YouTuber was Jack Doherty. And when the casino's boss was asked if the deal was real, he answered in public. Yes. Six months. Money well spent to get this off the internet.
shots.visual: Jack (stylised, blond hair, chain, sunglasses) stares at his phone in a gaming room; a big social-post card slides in beside him: 'Yes, it's real. 6-month term.'
shots.anim: Post card slides in; Jack's jaw drops; like counter starts climbing.

shots.vo: That reply got around two hundred and forty thousand likes. Roughly twenty-three times more than Jack's own post.
shots.visual: Two post cards side by side as a bar race: the CEO's post bar shoots up to 241K, Jack's stays tiny at ~10K.
shots.anim: Bars race; hearts burst from the tall one.

shots.vo: So how does someone become so disliked that paying him to disappear looks like good marketing? It starts, of all places, in a supermarket.
shots.visual: Exterior of a big supermarket at dusk; trolleys; Jack's silhouette walks towards the doors; a red KICKED OUT stamp waits above the door.
shots.onscreen: HOW DID IT COME TO THIS?
shots.anim: Camera pushes towards the doors; neon flickers.

shots.vo: This is the story of how getting kicked out became a business. And then a bill.
shots.visual: Title card: KICKED OUT FOR A LIVING; the BANNED clipboard appears top-right, empty.
shots.anim: Title slams in; stamp thump; clipboard slides in.

shots.vo: June twenty seventeen. A teenager and his friend Ricky film a floor-is-lava challenge inside a giant American supermarket. They leap from shelf to shelf, staff come running, and the two of them are thrown out.
shots.visual: Supermarket aisle: teen Jack and Ricky hop between shelf edges and a trolley; a staff member in a vest runs in waving; they get walked out.
shots.anim: Lava-red glow on the floor; boxes wobble; staff chase.

shots.vo: The video passes fifteen million views. And Jack learns the lesson that will shape the next nine years. Getting kicked out isn't the punishment. It's the product.
shots.visual: Teen bedroom: teen Jack at a laptop; a view counter rockets to 15,000,000; the red KICKED OUT stamp lands and turns gold like a trophy.
shots.anim: Counter rolls; stamp flips to gold.

shots.vo: Seven of his fifteen biggest videos have the supermarket or kicked out right in the title. His kicked-out uploads alone have pulled in around ninety million views.
shots.visual: A wall of video thumbnails (generic, no faces) in the creator room; seven of fifteen light up red; a counter adds to 90M.
shots.anim: Thumbnails flip red one by one; counter climbs.

shots.vo: The formula never changes. Do the stunt. Get removed. Post the clip. The security guard isn't the villain of the video. He's the free co-star.
shots.visual: Three-step loop on a shop floor: STUNT (Jack dances on a display), REMOVED (guard walks him out), POST (phone uploads); the guard gets a little 'CO-STAR' star badge.
shots.anim: Loop arrows spin; star badge pops on the guard.

shots.vo: By his twenties he has fifteen million subscribers, a garage of supercars, and a reputation. And the reputation is growing faster than the channel.
shots.visual: Glossy supercar showroom: adult Jack leans on a sleek orange supercar (no badge); a subscriber counter at 15M; a red REPUTATION bar overtakes the subscriber bar.

shots.vo: Slowly, the videos changed. Less pranking, more picking fights. He'd needle strangers in public, mocking them and their families, until somebody finally swung at him.
shots.visual: Shopping-mall concourse / street at day: Jack with a phone on a gimbal taunts a big man; speech bubbles of '!!!' and '#@%'; the man swings; Jack ducks behind the camera.

shots.vo: When one clip appeared to show him using a racial slur, he insisted the word was actually hater. Not long after, he aimed a different slur at his own fans.
shots.visual: A big clip-player frame on a dark background with a waveform bleeped out (a red BLEEP block); Jack beside it shrugs; a 'HE SAYS: "HATER"' tag.
shots.anim: Waveform pulses; bleep block slams down.

shots.vo: Around Halloween one year, a confrontation ended with a man knocked out. Jack posted that his security had done it. A lawsuit later alleged his guard was involved in the attack. His lawyers pushed back, and no outcome has been reported.
shots.visual: Courtroom: a lawsuit document marked ALLEGED slides onto the bench; Jack's lawyer pushes back with a hand; an 'OUTCOME: NOT REPORTED' tag.

shots.vo: More and more, he stood behind a wall of muscle. Before one stream, he told his security that if his guests tried to touch him, they shouldn't leave the property breathing.
shots.visual: Night, neon street: Jack peeks out from behind two huge bodyguards in black; a quote card slides in.

shots.vo: In June twenty twenty-four, he brawled with fellow streamer N3on at a fight night in Florida. The platform banned them both. N3on's verdict? Everyone just hates him.
shots.visual: Boxing arena with a ring: two streamers grapple ringside, phones flying; a ref pulls them apart; two BANNED tags drop.

shots.vo: And the muscle never left. In December twenty twenty-five, his crew clashed with former UFC heavyweight champion Andrei Arlovski at a boxing event. Each side blamed the other.
shots.visual: Same arena, different angle: a huge fighter (Arlovski, stylised) faces Jack's bodyguards; Jack points from behind; 'EACH SIDE BLAMES THE OTHER' tag.
shots.onscreen: DEC 2025 · EACH SIDE BLAMES THE OTHER

shots.vo: When Jack went live, he went to Kick. A platform launched in twenty twenty-two that sold itself to creators on one big promise. Fewer rules.
shots.visual: Bright tech-company atrium with a giant green LED wall reading KICK (plain text) and 'FEWER RULES'; streamers cheer.

shots.vo: But even Kick had a line. Weeks before what came next, after reports of its streamers harassing people at TwitchCon, several accounts were suspended.
shots.visual: Same atrium: a red velvet rope line is drawn across the floor; three streamer silhouettes get SUSPENDED tags.

shots.vo: Then, on the fifth of October twenty twenty-four, Jack went live from the driver's seat of a roughly two-hundred-thousand-dollar McLaren. On a wet highway near Miami.
shots.visual: Night highway in the rain, palm trees, guardrail; an orange supercar speeds past; LIVE badge pulses on a phone mount.

shots.vo: According to NBC News, the stream appeared to show him glancing down at the phone in his hand. Moments later, the car veered into a guardrail.
shots.visual: Inside-car style framing: Jack looks down at his phone; then the car slides and hits the guardrail; glass sparkles; screen shakes.

shots.vo: He posted the wreck himself. Crashed my McLaren, glad we're both okay. Viewers noticed he seemed more upset about the car than his cameraman, who needed stitches in his head. Jack later apologised to him.
shots.visual: Hospital bay: the cameraman with a head bandage on a bed; Jack stands looking at a phone photo of the crushed car; a post card 'Crashed my McLaren. Glad we're both okay.'
shots.anim: Heart monitor beeps; post card slides.

shots.vo: Kick banned him within hours, saying it doesn't condone illegal activity. And a Florida Highway Patrol crash report, obtained by the Miami New Times, gave him a citation for using his phone while driving.
shots.visual: Back at the atrium: the LED wall flips to BANNED; the clipboard gets line 1: KICK; a police citation slip flutters down.
shots.anim: Stamp thump; clipboard tick; paper flutter.

shots.vo: Days later he was live on TikTok, asking viewers to send him gifts, and explaining that he'd simply hydroplaned. Pouring rain. A McLaren. What did people expect?
shots.visual: Creator room: Jack streams on a vertical phone; gift icons (stars, galaxies) float up; a weather icon of pouring rain beside him.

shots.vo: Kick had called the ban permanent. It lasted three months. On the ninth of January twenty twenty-five, his channel was simply back, with no clear explanation. By then, Saturday Night Live had already parodied the crash.
shots.visual: TV studio stage: an actor in a blond wig in a cardboard car on a sketch set; studio audience laughs; a calendar flips to 9 JAN 2025; the clipboard's KICK line gets crossed out.

shots.vo: Nine days later, he was streaming in the street when a stranger walked straight up and slapped him.
shots.visual: Miami street by day: Jack streaming on a gimbal; a stranger walks in from the right and slaps him; phone wobbles.

shots.vo: According to Dexerto, Jack and his security chased the man down and beat him up. Kick banned him again. The same day.
shots.visual: Same street, wider: guards chase the stranger off-frame left; dust; the clipboard gets 'KICK (AGAIN)'.

shots.vo: His version? He'd defended himself, and the one time he stood up for himself, he got banned. His appeal was rejected. Two hundred thousand followers, and nowhere to stream to them.
shots.visual: Jack's bedroom studio at night: he types an appeal email; a REJECTED reply bounces back; a 200,000 follower counter greys out.
shots.anim: Email whoosh; reject buzz; counter greys.

shots.vo: So in February twenty twenty-six, he took the routine somewhere new. A golf tournament.
shots.visual: Sunny golf course with grandstands; Jack strolls in with sunglasses and a phone; polite golf crowd.

shots.vo: At the WM Phoenix Open, golf's rowdiest week, Jack offered a fan a hundred dollars to shout an insult in the middle of a player's backswing. The fan did it. Jack paid up.
shots.visual: Golf tee with a gallery rope: a golfer at the top of his backswing; a fan beside Jack cups his hands and shouts; a $100 note changes hands.

shots.vo: Security and police walked him out. An official told him, on camera, that he was trespassed from every future PGA Tour event. Jack asked: forever? For the foreseeable future, came the answer.
shots.visual: Golf course path: a police officer and a tournament official in a blazer walk Jack out; a TRESPASSED card; the clipboard gets 'PGA TOUR'.
shots.onscreen: TRESPASSED FROM ALL PGA TOUR EVENTS

shots.vo: Jack called it the most harmless prank he could have done. The golfer, Mackenzie Hughes, still made the cut, and said he didn't lose much sleep over it.
shots.visual: Split: Jack in his creator room shrugging to camera; the golfer on the green tips his cap; MADE THE CUT tag.

shots.vo: But look at the bill. A supermarket stunt costs you a supermarket. This one cost him an entire sport. Same pattern as twenty seventeen. The difference is that the places kicking him out had started keeping a list.
shots.visual: The BANNED clipboard fills the frame: SUPERMARKET, KICK, KICK (AGAIN), PGA TOUR; a pen adds a line; the paper keeps scrolling.

shots.vo: In late September twenty twenty-six, Jack asked on X whether he should stream on Kick and trade meme coins. The online casino Shuffle replied that it would pay him to stop talking.
shots.visual: Creator room: a big social post card from Jack ('Should I stream on Kick and trade meme coins?') and a reply card from SHUFFLE (plain text) 'We'll pay you to stop talking'.

shots.vo: According to IBTimes UK, a meme coin linked to Jack had fallen short of his hopes, and he went looking for sponsors to get his money up.
shots.visual: Chart: a meme-coin line (cartoon dog-free coin) rockets then nosedives; Jack's wallet empties; he scrolls sponsor offers.

shots.vo: Days later he posted a confession. He'd signed a contract with Shuffle without reading it fully. One clause said he couldn't post online any more. He thought it was a joke. Now they were enforcing it.
shots.visual: Law office: a long contract unrolls across the desk to the floor; a magnifier finds a clause 'NO POSTING'; Jack slaps his forehead.

shots.vo: Within an hour, Shuffle's boss confirmed it. Six months. Money well spent. The contract isn't public, so how far it really reaches is unclear, and Jack's lawyers are reportedly trying to get it scrapped.
shots.visual: Casino boardroom: the CEO (stylised, suit) smiles holding a phone; a post card 'Yes, it's real. 6-month term.'; the clipboard gets 'SHUFFLE (PAID)'; tag 'CONTRACT NOT PUBLIC'.

shots.vo: To be fair, he didn't vanish. A week later, he won a boxing match in Miami in about thirty seconds.
shots.visual: Boxing ring: Jack in gloves; opponent drops; ref waves it off; a 0:30 timer.

shots.vo: But look at the numbers. His twenty seventeen supermarket video, fifteen million views. His twenty twenty-three Island Boys video, eight point four million, and nothing since has beaten it. His latest upload? Around a hundred and twenty-five thousand.
shots.visual: Chart: three bars drop like a staircase: 15M (2017), 8.4M (2023), 125K (2026); Jack slides down them.

shots.vo: His subscriber count still says fifteen million. The subscribers stayed on paper. The views didn't.
shots.visual: Creator room at night: a plaque-like big 15M counter on the wall glows while a small view counter beside it flickers low; dust drifts.

shots.vo: And in his latest video, where he insists he's actually pretty chill, he walks a friend past a spot he's banned from. They just hate when I film here, he says. Nine years on, he still hasn't worked out why.
shots.visual: Back at the supermarket exterior at dusk: Jack and Ricky walk past; Jack points at the doors; the KICKED OUT stamp hovers; camera pulls back.
shots.onscreen: 'THEY JUST HATE WHEN I FILM HERE'

hooks: A casino paid a YouTuber with 15M subscribers to stop posting
Getting kicked out was the business model. Then came the bill
He crashed a $200,000 McLaren live, then asked for gifts
